---
title: "Predicting Hourly Precipitation at JFK Airport"
subtitle: "Regression comparison with temporal holdout evaluation"
author: "Miguelangel Palma Rojas"
date: last-modified
lang: en
---

## Objective

This notebook exposes the complete modeling workflow. It sorts observations by time, reserves the latest 20% for final evaluation, tunes ridge regression only on the earlier period, and compares every model on unseen data.

## Load packages


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
library(dplyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(here)
library(knitr)
library(readr)
library(tidymodels)
library(tidyr)
```
:::


## Read and validate weather data


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
weather <- read_csv(
  here("data", "jfk_weather_snapshot.csv"),
  show_col_types = FALSE,
  col_types = cols(date = col_datetime())
) |>
  arrange(date)

required_columns <- c(
  "date",
  "humidity",
  "temperature_f",
  "station_pressure",
  "wind_speed_mph",
  "precipitation_in"
)

missing_columns <- setdiff(required_columns, names(weather))

if (length(missing_columns) > 0) {
  stop(
    "Weather data is missing columns: ",
    paste(missing_columns, collapse = ", ")
  )
}

stopifnot(
  anyDuplicated(weather$date) == 0,
  !any(weather$precipitation_in < 0, na.rm = TRUE)
)

weather |>
  summarise(
    observations = n(),
    first_observation = min(date),
    last_observation = max(date),
    missing_predictor_cells = sum(
      is.na(across(where(is.numeric)))
    )
  ) |>
  kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


| observations|first_observation   |last_observation    | missing_predictor_cells|
|------------:|:-------------------|:-------------------|-----------------------:|
|         4067|2010-01-01 04:51:00 |2018-07-26 10:51:00 |                       4|


:::
:::



::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ggplot(weather, aes(x = precipitation_in)) +
  geom_histogram(
    binwidth = 0.01,
    boundary = 0,
    fill = "#2A9D8F",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  coord_cartesian(
    xlim = c(
      0,
      quantile(weather$precipitation_in, 0.995, na.rm = TRUE)
    )
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Hourly precipitation is strongly zero-inflated",
    x = "Precipitation (inches)",
    y = "Observations"

```

## Exploratory analysis

The predictors operate on different scales. Faceted histograms reveal skewness, concentration, and potential measurement artifacts before modeling.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
weather |>
  select(
    humidity,
    temperature_f,
    station_pressure,
    wind_speed_mph
  ) |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = everything(),
    names_to = "predictor",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = value)) +
  geom_histogram(
    bins = 30,
    fill = "#2A9D8F",
    color = "white"
  ) +
  facet_wrap(
    vars(predictor),
    scales = "free",
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  labs(
    title = "Weather predictor distributions",
    x = NULL,
    y = "Observations"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/predictor-distributions-1.png){fig-alt='Faceted histograms showing the distributions of humidity, temperature, station pressure, and wind speed.' width=672}
:::
:::


Daily aggregation makes wet periods visible without drawing thousands of hourly points.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
daily_precipitation <- weather |>
  mutate(day = as.Date(date)) |>
  group_by(day) |>
  summarise(
    precipitation_in = sum(precipitation_in, na.rm = TRUE),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(
  daily_precipitation,
  aes(x = day, y = precipitation_in)
) +
  geom_col(fill = "#457B9D", width = 1) +
  labs(
    title = "Daily precipitation varies in short, irregular episodes",
    x = "Date",
    y = "Daily precipitation (inches)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/precipitation-time-series-1.png){fig-alt='Daily precipitation totals at JFK through the observed period.' width=672}
:::
:::


## Create training, tuning, and test sets


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
set.seed(2026)

weather_split <- initial_time_split(weather, prop = 0.8)
training_data <- training(weather_split)
testing_data <- testing(weather_split)
resamples <- vfold_cv(training_data, v = 5)

tibble(
  partition = c("Training and tuning", "Final test"),
  observations = c(nrow(training_data), nrow(testing_data)),
  first_date = c(min(training_data$date), min(testing_data$date)),
  last_date = c(max(training_data$date), max(testing_data$date))
) |>
  kable()
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|partition           | observations|first_date          |last_date           |
|:-------------------|------------:|:-------------------|:-------------------|
|Training and tuning |         3253|2010-01-01 04:51:00 |2016-11-05 18:51:00 |
|Final test          |          814|2016-11-05 22:51:00 |2018-07-26 10:51:00 |


:::
:::


## Mean baseline


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
baseline_predictions <- testing_data |>
  transmute(
    precipitation_in,
    .pred = mean(training_data$precipitation_in)
  )
```
:::


## Shared preprocessing recipe

Median imputation and normalization are estimated inside each workflow, so the final test period cannot influence preprocessing.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
weather_recipe <- recipe(
  precipitation_in ~
    humidity +
    temperature_f +
    station_pressure +
    wind_speed_mph,
  data = training_data
) |>
  step_impute_median(all_numeric_predictors()) |>
  step_normalize(all_numeric_predictors())
```
:::


## Linear regression


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
linear_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(weather_recipe) |>
  add_model(
    linear_reg() |>
      set_engine("lm")
  )

linear_fit <- fit(linear_workflow, data = training_data)

linear_predictions <- bind_cols(
  testing_data |> select(precipitation_in),
  predict(linear_fit, new_data = testing_data)
)
```
:::


## Ridge regression with cross-validation


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ridge_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(weather_recipe) |>
  add_model(
    linear_reg(
      penalty = tune(),
      mixture = 0
    ) |>
      set_engine("glmnet")
  )

ridge_grid <- grid_regular(
  penalty(range = c(-5, 0)),
  levels = 8
)

ridge_results <- tune_grid(
  ridge_workflow,
  resamples = resamples,
  grid = ridge_grid,
  metrics = metric_set(rmse, mae, rsq_trad)
)

best_penalty <- select_best(ridge_results, metric = "rmse")
best_penalty |> kable(digits = 5)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


| penalty|.config         |
|-------:|:---------------|
|  0.0072|pre0_mod5_post0 |


:::

```{.r .cell-code}
ridge_fit <- ridge_workflow |>
  finalize_workflow(best_penalty) |>
  fit(data = training_data)

ridge_predictions <- bind_cols(
  testing_data |> select(precipitation_in),
  predict(ridge_fit, new_data = testing_data)
)
```
:::


The tuning profile shows whether the selected penalty lies in a stable region or at the edge of the search grid.


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
ridge_tuning <- ridge_results |>
  collect_metrics() |>
  filter(.metric == "rmse")

ggplot(
  ridge_tuning,
  aes(x = penalty, y = mean)
) +
  geom_ribbon(
    aes(
      ymin = mean - std_err,
      ymax = mean + std_err
    ),
    fill = "#A8DADC",
    alpha = 0.6
  ) +
  geom_line(color = "#1D3557", linewidth = 0.9) +
  geom_point(color = "#1D3557", size = 2) +
  scale_x_log10() +
  labs(
    title = "Ridge penalty selected through cross-validation",
    x = "Penalty (log scale)",
    y = "Cross-validation RMSE"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/ridge-tuning-curve-1.png){fig-alt='Cross-validation RMSE across ridge penalty values.' width=672}
:::
:::


## Polynomial regression


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
polynomial_recipe <- weather_recipe |>
  step_poly(
    temperature_f,
    humidity,
    station_pressure,
    wind_speed_mph,
    degree = 2
  )

polynomial_workflow <- workflow() |>
  add_recipe(polynomial_recipe) |>
  add_model(
    linear_reg() |>
      set_engine("lm")
  )

polynomial_fit <- fit(
  polynomial_workflow,
  data = training_data
)

polynomial_predictions <- bind_cols(
  testing_data |> select(precipitation_in),
  predict(polynomial_fit, new_data = testing_data)
)
```
:::


## Final holdout performance


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
baseline_metrics <- bind_rows(
  rmse(baseline_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred),
  mae(baseline_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred),
  rsq_trad(baseline_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred)
) |>
  mutate(model = "Mean baseline")

linear_metrics <- bind_rows(
  rmse(linear_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred),
  mae(linear_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred),
  rsq_trad(linear_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred)
) |>
  mutate(model = "Linear regression")

ridge_metrics <- bind_rows(
  rmse(ridge_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred),
  mae(ridge_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred),
  rsq_trad(ridge_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred)
) |>
  mutate(model = "Ridge regression")

polynomial_metrics <- bind_rows(
  rmse(polynomial_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred),
  mae(polynomial_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred),
  rsq_trad(polynomial_predictions, precipitation_in, .pred)
) |>
  mutate(model = "Polynomial regression")

holdout_metrics <- bind_rows(
  baseline_metrics,
  linear_metrics,
  ridge_metrics,
  polynomial_metrics
) |>
  select(model, .metric, .estimate)

holdout_metrics |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = .metric,
    values_from = .estimate
  ) |>
  arrange(rmse) |>
  kable(digits = 4)
```

::: {.cell-output-display}


|model                 |   rmse|    mae| rsq_trad|
|:---------------------|------:|------:|--------:|
|Polynomial regression | 0.0444| 0.0146|   0.0604|
|Linear regression     | 0.0447| 0.0140|   0.0510|
|Ridge regression      | 0.0447| 0.0132|   0.0498|
|Mean baseline         | 0.0458| 0.0120|   0.0000|


:::
:::


RMSE emphasizes larger misses, MAE describes typical absolute error, and R² measures improvement relative to a constant mean on the same holdout.

## Observed versus predicted


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
prediction_comparison <- bind_rows(
  baseline_predictions |>
    mutate(model = "Mean baseline"),
  linear_predictions |>
    mutate(model = "Linear regression"),
  ridge_predictions |>
    mutate(model = "Ridge regression"),
  polynomial_predictions |>
    mutate(model = "Polynomial regression")
) |>
  mutate(
    model = factor(
      model,
      levels = c(
        "Mean baseline",
        "Linear regression",
        "Ridge regression",
        "Polynomial regression"
      )
    )
  )

wet_prediction_comparison <- prediction_comparison |>
  filter(precipitation_in > 0)

ggplot(
  wet_prediction_comparison,
  aes(x = precipitation_in, y = .pred)
) +
  geom_abline(
    slope = 1,
    intercept = 0,
    color = "#E76F51",
    linewidth = 0.8
  ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.35, color = "#2A9D8F") +
  facet_wrap(
    vars(model),
    scales = "free_y",
    ncol = 2
  ) +
  scale_x_sqrt() +
  scale_y_sqrt() +
  labs(
    title = "Observed and predicted precipitation during wet holdout hours",
    x = "Observed precipitation (inches)",
    y = "Predicted precipitation (inches)"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/observed-predicted-1.png){fig-alt='Faceted observed-versus-predicted plots for wet hours across the four precipitation models.' width=672}
:::
:::


## Residual comparison


::: {.cell}

```{.r .cell-code}
residual_comparison <- prediction_comparison |>
  mutate(residual = precipitation_in - .pred)

ggplot(
  residual_comparison,
  aes(x = .pred, y = residual)
) +
  geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "#555555") +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.3, color = "#457B9D") +
  geom_smooth(se = FALSE, color = "#E76F51") +
  facet_wrap(vars(model), scales = "free_x", ncol = 2) +
  labs(
    title = "Residual structure reveals systematic underprediction",
    x = "Predicted precipitation (inches)",
    y = "Observed minus predicted"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 12) +
  theme(plot.title = element_text(face = "bold"))
```

::: {.cell-output-display}
![](index_files/figure-html/residual-comparison-1.png){fig-alt='Faceted residual plots for the four precipitation models.' width=672}
:::
:::


## Conclusion

The visible code demonstrates temporal splitting, leakage-safe preprocessing, cross-validation, hyperparameter selection, prediction, and final evaluation. See the [Spanish version](es/index.qmd).
